extracted.intended_audience: Board of Control / Court of Directors of the East India Company; British government policymakers and administrators concerned with Indian revenues and Company governance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and contested policy positions concerning (a) the treatment and computation of the Nabob of Arcot's private and public debts and revenues, and (b) rules of conduct and enforcement for Company servants and British subjects interacting with native powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on loans by Company servants
rubrics_metrics.description: “no person, being a servant of the Company, or being under our protection, shall, on any pretence whatever, be concerned in any loan or other money transaction with any of the country powers, unless with the knowledge and express permission of our respective governments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any servant discovered counteracting this order should be sent home to England at the first opportunity and punished as guilty of disobedience; the Company will give no protection or assistance for recovery of any loans connected with such transactions; connivance will incur the highest displeasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob/family
rubrics_metrics.description: “we repeat our prohibition in the strongest terms respecting any intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is justified because such intercourse has been carried on to the detriment and expense of the Nabob and merely to the advantage of individuals; those offending the letter and spirit of this order, whether in the Company's service or under their protection, are to be forthwith sent to England.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement policy for breaches by protected persons
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of our servants, or others, being under our protection, shall be discovered in any respect counteracting these orders, we strictly enjoin you to take the first opportunity of sending them home to England, to be punished as guilty of disobedience of orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No protection or assistance of the Company shall be given for the recovery of any loans connected with such transactions; particular attention is strictly enjoined and connivance will incur highest displeasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve opportunity to question justice of listed debts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court submits that at least the opportunity of questioning, within the limited time, the justice of any of the debts, ought to have been fully preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if many debts fall into classes believed free from imputation, discussion of disputed debts causes no injury to individuals and is required by the act's direction to examine the nature and origin of the debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine nature/origin of debts and interest rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry should be made into the nature and origin of the debts and, in particular, the rate of interest according to which debts arising from soucar assignment of the land-revenues to servants (acting as native bankers) have been accumulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also examine the reasonableness of the deduction of twenty-five per cent directed by the Bengal government from a great part of the debts on certain conditions; these are substantive investigatory matters required by the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company's priority claim for arrears of expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our right to be paid the arrears of those expenses by which, almost to our own ruin, we have preserved the country and all the property connected with it from falling a prey to a foreign conqueror, surely stands paramount to all claims for former debts upon the revenues of a country so preserved.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the Company's debt shall be discharged, it will not consent to give up any part of the sums (e.g. seven lacs of pagodas) to private creditors; this asserts a priority of public/Company claims over private creditor claims on revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of debts with simple interest only
rubrics_metrics.description: “It was not our intention to allow [compound interest]; ... we have added an express direction that the debts be made up with simple interest only, from the time of their respective consolidation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit instruction (see Clause F f.) to avoid compounding interest when making up the amount of private debts; intended to prevent inflated debt totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on local revenue estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioners place the greatest reliance on the estimate transmitted by your President of Fort St. George, having there the best means of information upon the fact, and stating it with a particular view to the subject matter of these paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some allowance should be made for differences of collection in the Nabob's hands, but local informed estimates are treated as the best basis for computing expected revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional payment rule if revenue deficiency occurs
rubrics_metrics.description: If, notwithstanding the provisions contained in our former paragraphs, any deficiency should arise, the payments of what shall be received shall be made in the same proportion which would have obtained in the division of the whole twelve lacs, had they been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This directive prevents a deficiency from falling wholly on any one class of debts by ensuring received sums are distributed according to the originally proposed proportions.
